q19327.en: The sign shown warns that wild animals will probably cross.

explain.short: The leaping deer is the 'animali selvatici' (wild animals) sign: wild animals may cross the road ahead.
explain.rule: 'Animali selvatici' (wild animals) is a danger sign: wild animals may cross suddenly. Slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'probabile' means likely: the sign warns of a possibility, not a certainty.

q19328.en: The sign shown requires you to slow down and, if needed, to stop if the animals show signs of fear.

explain.short: A frightened animal can jump in any direction, so you slow down and stop if needed.
explain.rule: 'Animali selvatici' (wild animals) is a danger sign: wild animals may cross suddenly. Slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'all'occorrenza' means 'if needed': you stop only when the situation requires it.

sceneParams.caption: Slow down; stop if animals get scared

q19329.en: The sign shown requires you to slow down and, if needed, to stop if the animals suddenly cross the road.

explain.short: An animal can jump onto the road at any moment, so you slow down and are ready to stop.
explain.rule: 'Animali selvatici' (wild animals) is a danger sign: wild animals may cross suddenly. Slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'improvvisamente' (suddenly) is the real danger: you cannot predict it, so you drive slowly.

sceneParams.caption: Slow down; stop if animals cross

q19330.en: The sign shown warns that you may suddenly find stray animals on the carriageway.

explain.short: Wild animals can appear on the road without warning, and this sign tells you to expect them.
explain.rule: 'Animali selvatici' (wild animals) is a danger sign: wild animals may cross suddenly. Slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'vaganti' means wandering freely: animals moving on their own, nobody leads them.

sceneParams.caption: Animals may appear on the road

q19331.en: The sign shown warns of the likely and sudden crossing of wild animals.

explain.short: The deer means wild animals may cross, often without any warning.
explain.rule: 'Animali selvatici' (wild animals) is a danger sign: wild animals may cross suddenly. Slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'probabile e improvviso' (likely and sudden): both words fit this danger.

q19332.en: The sign shown requires you to slow down to avoid hitting wandering wild animals.

explain.short: Going slowly gives you time to brake if an animal comes onto the road.
explain.rule: 'Animali selvatici' (wild animals) is a danger sign: wild animals may cross suddenly. Slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'per evitare urti' (to avoid collisions) is the reason for slowing down: correct.

sceneParams.caption: Slow down to avoid hitting animals

q19333.en: When you see the sign shown, you must repeatedly use the horn to scare the animals away.

explain.short: The horn can scare animals and make them jump in front of you; the sign asks you to slow down, not to honk.
explain.rule: 'Animali selvatici' (wild animals) is a danger sign: wild animals may cross suddenly. Slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'obbligatorio' (compulsory) and 'ripetutamente' (repeatedly): no rule makes you honk here.

sceneParams.caption: Slow down - no need to honk

q19334.en: The sign shown warns of an area reserved for the movement of wild animals.

explain.short: The road is a normal road for everyone; the sign only warns that animals may cross it.
explain.rule: 'Animali selvatici' (wild animals) is a danger sign: wild animals may cross suddenly. Slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'riservata' (reserved) is wrong: nothing is reserved for animals.

sceneParams.caption: Animals may cross - not a reserved area

q19335.en: The sign shown obliges you to drive in the middle of the road to avoid running over wild animals.

explain.short: You keep to the right as usual and slow down; driving in the middle is dangerous and never required.
explain.rule: 'Animali selvatici' (wild animals) is a danger sign: wild animals may cross suddenly. Slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'obbliga a marciare al centro' (obliges you to drive in the middle): no such duty exists.

keywords.en: in the middle of the road

q19336.en: The sign shown allows only four-wheel-drive vehicles to pass.

explain.short: It is a danger warning, not a restriction: every vehicle may drive on this road.
explain.rule: 'Animali selvatici' (wild animals) is a danger sign: wild animals may cross suddenly. Slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'soli' (only): the sign does not limit who may pass.

sceneParams.caption: A warning for everyone, not 4x4 only

q19337.en: The sign shown marks the entrance of a safari zoo.

explain.short: A red-edged triangle is always a danger warning: here, wild animals may cross.
explain.rule: 'Animali selvatici' (wild animals) is a danger sign: wild animals may cross suddenly. Slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'zoo safari' sounds right because of the animal, but the sign is a danger warning.

sceneParams.caption: Wild animals may cross - not a zoo

q19338.en: The sign shown marks the entrance of a National Park.

explain.short: A red-edged triangle is a danger warning, not an entrance sign: wild animals may cross.
explain.rule: 'Animali selvatici' (wild animals) is a danger sign: wild animals may cross suddenly. Slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'ingresso' (entrance): danger signs never mark an entrance to a place.

sceneParams.caption: Wild animals may cross - not a park

q19339.en: The sign shown warns that a one-way carriageway becomes two-way.

explain.short: The two opposite arrows mean that after this point traffic flows in both directions.
explain.rule: 'Doppio senso di circolazione' (two-way traffic) is a danger sign: the one-way stretch ends and oncoming vehicles will appear.
explain.trap: 'diventa a doppio senso' (becomes two-way): correct, the one-way stretch ends.

q19340.en: The sign shown warns that, a little further on, you may meet vehicles travelling in the opposite direction.

explain.short: The arrow pointing down is the oncoming traffic you will soon meet.
explain.rule: 'Doppio senso di circolazione' (two-way traffic) is a danger sign: the one-way stretch ends and oncoming vehicles will appear.
explain.trap: 'senso opposto' (opposite direction): the vehicles coming towards you.

q19341.en: The sign shown warns that the one-way traffic ends.

explain.short: Two-way traffic starts, so the one-way stretch is over.
explain.rule: 'Doppio senso di circolazione' (two-way traffic) is a danger sign: the one-way stretch ends and oncoming vehicles will appear.
explain.trap: 'termina' (ends): the one-way ends and two-way begins.

q19342.en: The sign shown is a danger sign.

explain.short: A triangle with a red border is the shape of danger signs: here, oncoming traffic.
explain.rule: 'Doppio senso di circolazione' (two-way traffic) is a danger sign: the one-way stretch ends and oncoming vehicles will appear.
explain.trap: 'pericolo' (danger): the triangle shape tells you the category.

q19343.en: The sign shown indicates that, a little further on, you will need to be more careful.

explain.short: Every danger sign asks for more care: here, vehicles will come towards you.
explain.rule: 'Doppio senso di circolazione' (two-way traffic) is a danger sign: the one-way stretch ends and oncoming vehicles will appear.
explain.trap: 'occorrerà' means 'it will be necessary': care is needed after the sign.

q19344.en: The sign shown, if on a yellow background, is placed where roadworks are in progress.

explain.short: Yellow signs are temporary signs for roadworks; works often make traffic two-way on one carriageway.
explain.rule: 'Doppio senso di circolazione' (two-way traffic) is a danger sign: the one-way stretch ends and oncoming vehicles will appear.
explain.trap: 'se a fondo giallo' (if yellow background): yellow signs belong to roadworks.

q19345.en: When you see the sign shown, overtaking, if allowed, must be done with particular care.

explain.short: Oncoming vehicles may appear, so an overtake needs extra care.
explain.rule: 'Doppio senso di circolazione' (two-way traffic) is a danger sign: the one-way stretch ends and oncoming vehicles will appear.
explain.trap: 'se consentito' (if allowed): the sign does not ban overtaking, it asks for care.

q19346.en: The sign shown warns that traffic runs on two separate carriageways.

explain.short: Both directions share the SAME carriageway, with nothing between them.
explain.rule: 'Doppio senso di circolazione' (two-way traffic) is a danger sign: the one-way stretch ends and oncoming vehicles will appear.
explain.trap: 'due carreggiate separate' (two separate carriageways) is the opposite situation.

q19347.en: The sign shown warns that traffic becomes one-way.

explain.short: It is the opposite: the one-way ends and traffic becomes two-way.
explain.rule: 'Doppio senso di circolazione' (two-way traffic) is a danger sign: the one-way stretch ends and oncoming vehicles will appear.
explain.trap: 'senso unico' (one-way) is the opposite of what the arrows show.

q19348.en: The sign shown requires you to give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

explain.short: This sign gives no priority rule; it only warns of oncoming traffic. Giving way to oncoming traffic is a round sign with a red and a black arrow.
explain.rule: 'Doppio senso di circolazione' (two-way traffic) is a danger sign: the one-way stretch ends and oncoming vehicles will appear.
explain.trap: 'impone di dare la precedenza' (requires you to give way): a danger sign gives no priority order.

q19349.en: The sign shown announces right of way on alternating one-way stretches.

explain.short: Right of way on an alternating one-way stretch is a square blue sign; this red triangle only warns of two-way traffic.
explain.rule: 'Doppio senso di circolazione' (two-way traffic) is a danger sign: the one-way stretch ends and oncoming vehicles will appear.
explain.trap: 'diritto di precedenza' (right of way): that is a different, blue sign.

sceneParams.caption: Two-way traffic, not right of way

q19350.en: The sign shown warns that you must turn back.

explain.short: You can go on: the sign only warns that vehicles will come towards you.
explain.rule: 'Doppio senso di circolazione' (two-way traffic) is a danger sign: the one-way stretch ends and oncoming vehicles will appear.
explain.trap: 'ritornare indietro' (turn back): the down arrow is oncoming traffic, not an order to turn round.

sceneParams.caption: Go on carefully - no need to turn back

q19351.en: The sign shown warns of an alternating one-way stretch.

explain.short: Alternating one-way means one direction at a time; here both directions flow at the same time.
explain.rule: 'Doppio senso di circolazione' (two-way traffic) is a danger sign: the one-way stretch ends and oncoming vehicles will appear.
explain.trap: 'senso unico alternato' (alternating one-way) is a different situation, with different signs.

sceneParams.caption: Both ways at once, not alternating

q19352.en: The sign shown is an advance warning of a compulsory direction.

explain.short: Compulsory directions are round blue signs; this red triangle warns of oncoming traffic.
explain.rule: 'Doppio senso di circolazione' (two-way traffic) is a danger sign: the one-way stretch ends and oncoming vehicles will appear.
explain.trap: 'direzione obbligatoria' (compulsory direction): the arrows here are not an order.

sceneParams.caption: Danger sign, not a direction order

q19353.en: The sign shown warns that the road leads onto a harbour quay.

explain.short: The car at the edge above the water means the road ends at water, for example on a harbour quay.
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'banchina' usually means the road shoulder, but 'banchina portuale' is a harbour quay.

sceneParams.caption: Road ends on a quay: risk of water

keywords.en: end, outlet (where the road comes out)

q19354.en: The sign shown warns that the road leads onto a pier.

explain.short: The road ends at the water, and a pier (molo) is one such place.
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'molo' means pier, a structure going out into the water.

sceneParams.caption: Road ends on a pier: risk of water

q19355.en: The sign shown warns that the road leads onto a river bank.

explain.short: The sign is used where the road ends on water, including a river bank (argine).
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'argine' means the raised bank along a river.

sceneParams.caption: Road ends on a river bank

q19356.en: The sign shown warns that the road leads onto a canal bank.

explain.short: A canal bank also means water right next to the road: the same danger.
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'canale' (canal) works as well as 'fiume' (river): any water at the end of the road.

sceneParams.caption: Road ends on a canal bank

q19357.en: When you see the sign shown, you must take particular care, especially at night, to avoid falling into the water.

explain.short: In the dark the edge of the water is hard to see, so extra care is needed.
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'soprattutto di notte' (especially at night): darkness hides the edge.

sceneParams.caption: Extra care at night: water ahead

q19358.en: The sign shown warns of the danger of falling into water.

explain.short: The car tipping over the edge into the water shows exactly this danger.
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'caduta in acqua' (falling into water): that is the picture on the sign.

q19359.en: When you see the sign shown, you must take particular care if, on the stretch that follows, you will have to reverse.

explain.short: On a quay or bank you may need to turn or reverse near the edge; one mistake and the car ends in the water.
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'retromarcia' (reversing): when reversing you see the edge badly, so it is very risky here.

q19360.en: The sign shown is a danger sign.

explain.short: A triangle with a red border is a danger sign: here, water at the end of the road.
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'pericolo' (danger): the triangle shape tells you the category.

q19361.en: The sign shown warns of a viaduct under construction.

explain.short: The picture shows a car going off an edge into water, not a bridge being built.
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'viadotto in costruzione' (viaduct being built): nothing in the picture shows works.

sceneParams.caption: Water at road's end, not a viaduct

q19362.en: The sign shown obliges you to stop at a moving bridge in operation.

explain.short: It is a warning, not a stop order; a moving bridge has its own, different danger sign.
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'obbliga ad arrestarsi' (obliges you to stop): danger signs warn, they do not order a stop.

sceneParams.caption: Warning about water, no stop order

q19363.en: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road cut off by flooding.

explain.short: The water is a quay, bank or canal at the road's end, not a flood on the road.
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'alluvione' (flood): the water in the picture is a permanent quay or bank.

sceneParams.caption: Quay or bank, not a flood

q19364.en: The sign shown warns that the road leads onto a moving bridge.

explain.short: A moving bridge has its own sign; this one means a quay or a river bank.
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'ponte mobile' (moving bridge) is a different danger sign.

sceneParams.caption: Quay or bank, not a moving bridge

q19365.en: When you see the sign shown, you must take particular care because there is a steep descent.

explain.short: A steep descent has its own sign with a percentage; this one warns of water at the road's end.
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'discesa ripida' (steep descent) is a different sign.

sceneParams.caption: Water ahead, not a steep descent

q19366.en: The sign shown warns of the danger of sea storms.

explain.short: The sign warns of the road ending at water, not of storms or waves.
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'mareggiate' (sea storms): the waves in the picture only mean water.

sceneParams.caption: Water at road's end, not storms

q19367.en: The sign shown warns of an area equipped for washing vehicles.

explain.short: The car and the water do not mean a car wash: it is a red danger triangle.
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'lavaggio dei veicoli' (car wash): a danger sign never points to a service.

sceneParams.caption: Danger of water, not a car wash

q19368.en: The sign shown refers only to cars.

explain.short: Danger signs are for all road users, whatever vehicle they drive.
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'soltanto' (only): the car is just a drawing, the sign is for everyone.

q19369.en: The sign shown is not valid in the summer months.

explain.short: The quay or river bank is there all year, so the sign is always valid.
explain.rule: This danger sign means the road leads onto a quay or a river/canal bank: risk of falling into the water.
explain.trap: 'non ha validità' (is not valid): no season switches this danger off.

q19370.en: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road where the vehicle's grip may decrease.

explain.short: Loose gravel works like small balls under the tyres, so grip gets worse.
explain.rule: 'Materiale instabile' (loose chippings) is a danger sign: loose gravel reduces grip and can be thrown by tyres.
explain.trap: 'aderenza' means grip of the tyres on the road.

q19371.en: The sign shown requires you to proceed with caution near pedestrians, even if they are off the carriageway.

explain.short: Your tyres can throw stones sideways and hit people walking beside the road.
explain.rule: 'Materiale instabile' (loose chippings) is a danger sign: loose gravel reduces grip and can be thrown by tyres.
explain.trap: 'anche se fuori dalla carreggiata' (even if off the carriageway): thrown stones can reach them.

q19372.en: The sign shown warns of chippings that can be thrown a distance as the vehicle passes.

explain.short: The picture shows exactly this: a car throwing small stones behind it.
explain.rule: 'Materiale instabile' (loose chippings) is a danger sign: loose gravel reduces grip and can be thrown by tyres.
explain.trap: 'scagliato a distanza' (thrown a distance): that is what the picture shows.

sceneParams.caption: Chippings can be thrown by tyres

q19373.en: The sign shown requires you to reduce speed when meeting another vehicle.

explain.short: When you pass an oncoming vehicle, stones from your tyres or theirs can break a windscreen.
explain.rule: 'Materiale instabile' (loose chippings) is a danger sign: loose gravel reduces grip and can be thrown by tyres.
explain.trap: 'incrociando' means meeting a vehicle coming the other way.

q19374.en: When you see the sign shown, it is wise to keep a greater distance from the vehicle in front.

explain.short: More distance keeps you away from stones thrown by the car in front, and gives more room to brake with less grip.
explain.rule: 'Materiale instabile' (loose chippings) is a danger sign: loose gravel reduces grip and can be thrown by tyres.
explain.trap: 'opportuno' (wise, advisable): a sensible behaviour, correct here.

q19375.en: The sign shown warns of the danger of finding chippings on the road surface.

explain.short: Loose gravel on the road is exactly what this sign means.
explain.rule: 'Materiale instabile' (loose chippings) is a danger sign: loose gravel reduces grip and can be thrown by tyres.
explain.trap: 'pietrisco' means small loose stones, gravel chippings.

q19376.en: When you see the sign shown, you must consider the danger of skidding or sliding.

explain.short: With less grip the car can slide, above all when braking or turning.
explain.rule: 'Materiale instabile' (loose chippings) is a danger sign: loose gravel reduces grip and can be thrown by tyres.
explain.trap: 'sbandamento o slittamento' (skidding or sliding): both come from lost grip.

q19377.en: The sign shown, if on a yellow background, is placed where there are roadworks.

explain.short: Yellow signs are temporary signs for roadworks, where loose gravel is common.
explain.rule: 'Materiale instabile' (loose chippings) is a danger sign: loose gravel reduces grip and can be thrown by tyres.
explain.trap: 'se a fondo giallo' (if yellow background): yellow signs belong to roadworks.

q19378.en: The sign shown advises you to accelerate to increase the vehicle's grip on the asphalt.

explain.short: Accelerating on gravel makes grip worse and throws more stones: you must slow down.
explain.rule: 'Materiale instabile' (loose chippings) is a danger sign: loose gravel reduces grip and can be thrown by tyres.
explain.trap: 'accelerare' (accelerate) is the opposite of what you must do.

q19379.en: The sign shown is a prescription sign.

explain.short: A red-edged triangle is a danger sign; prescription signs (orders and bans) are mostly round.
explain.rule: 'Materiale instabile' (loose chippings) is a danger sign: loose gravel reduces grip and can be thrown by tyres.
explain.trap: 'prescrizione' (prescription, an order or ban): wrong category.

q19380.en: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road at risk of landslide.

explain.short: The picture shows small stones thrown by a car, not earth sliding down.
explain.rule: 'Materiale instabile' (loose chippings) is a danger sign: loose gravel reduces grip and can be thrown by tyres.
explain.trap: 'frana' (landslide): that is closer to the falling rocks sign.

q19381.en: The sign shown, if on a yellow background, warns of a stretch of road that cannot be used because of roadworks.

explain.short: The yellow version marks roadworks, but you can still drive through, carefully.
explain.rule: 'Materiale instabile' (loose chippings) is a danger sign: loose gravel reduces grip and can be thrown by tyres.
explain.trap: 'non percorribile' (cannot be used): the road stays open.

sceneParams.caption: Roadworks, but the road is open

q19382.en: The sign shown warns of soft verges.

explain.short: Soft verges have their own sign; this one shows loose gravel thrown by tyres.
explain.rule: 'Materiale instabile' (loose chippings) is a danger sign: loose gravel reduces grip and can be thrown by tyres.
explain.trap: 'banchine cedevoli' (soft verges, edges that sink) is a different danger.

q19383.en: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road where there is a danger of falling rocks.

explain.short: Falling rocks has a different picture, with a rock face; here a car throws up gravel.
explain.rule: 'Materiale instabile' (loose chippings) is a danger sign: loose gravel reduces grip and can be thrown by tyres.
explain.trap: 'caduta di massi' (falling rocks) is a different sign.

q19384.en: The sign shown announces the obligation to fit snow chains.

explain.short: Snow chains are a round blue order sign; this triangle warns of loose gravel.
explain.rule: 'Materiale instabile' (loose chippings) is a danger sign: loose gravel reduces grip and can be thrown by tyres.
explain.trap: 'obbligo' (obligation): danger signs give no obligation like this.

q19385.en: The sign shown warns of the danger of falling rocks.

explain.short: The rock face with stones dropping is the 'caduta massi' (falling rocks) sign.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the left, so stones come from the left.
explain.trap: 'massi' means rocks, big stones.

q19386.en: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road where stones may be on the carriageway.

explain.short: Fallen stones can lie on the road after they drop from the rock face.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the left, so stones come from the left.
explain.trap: 'presenza di pietre' (stones present): the result of falling rocks.

sceneParams.caption: Stones may be on the road

q19387.en: The sign shown warns of the danger of stones falling from the left and so being on the carriageway.

explain.short: In this picture the rock face is on the LEFT, so stones fall from the left.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the left, so stones come from the left.
explain.trap: 'da sinistra' (from the left): check which side the rock face is on.

q19388.en: When you see the sign shown, it is wise to reduce speed to avoid hitting any rocks fallen on the carriageway.

explain.short: Going slowly lets you see and avoid a stone in time.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the left, so stones come from the left.
explain.trap: 'opportuno' (wise): slowing down is the right reaction here.

sceneParams.caption: Slow down to avoid fallen rocks

q19389.en: When you see the sign shown, it is advisable to avoid long stops on the stretch of road where the danger is.

explain.short: Stones can fall at any moment, so do not stay long under the rock face.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the left, so stones come from the left.
explain.trap: 'lunghe soste' (long stops): staying under the rocks increases the risk.

sceneParams.caption: Don't stop long under the rocks

q19390.en: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road with roadworks.

explain.short: Roadworks have their own sign (a worker with a shovel); this one shows falling rocks.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the left, so stones come from the left.
explain.trap: 'cantieri stradali' (roadworks) is a different sign.

q19391.en: When you see the sign shown, it is wise to sound the horn insistently.

explain.short: The horn does not stop rocks: you must slow down and watch the road.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the left, so stones come from the left.
explain.trap: 'suonare con insistenza' (honk insistently): useless and not allowed without need.

q19392.en: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road in bad condition or with an irregular surface.

explain.short: A bad road surface is the 'strada deformata' sign; this one shows falling rocks.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the left, so stones come from the left.
explain.trap: 'cattivo stato' (bad condition): that is the uneven-road sign.

sceneParams.caption: Falling rocks, not a bad surface

q19393.en: The sign shown warns of a stretch of uneven road.

explain.short: 'Strada deformata' has a wavy line; this sign has a rock face and falling stones.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the left, so stones come from the left.
explain.trap: 'deformata' (uneven): a different sign.

q19394.en: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road where overtaking is forbidden.

explain.short: A danger sign does not ban overtaking; no-overtaking is a round sign with two cars.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the left, so stones come from the left.
explain.trap: 'vietato il sorpasso' (overtaking forbidden): a different, round sign.

q19395.en: The sign shown warns of the danger of rocks falling from the right.

explain.short: In this picture the rock face is on the RIGHT, so rocks fall from the right.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the right, so stones come from the right.
explain.trap: 'da destra' (from the right): check which side the rock face is on.

q19396.en: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road where stones may be on the carriageway.

explain.short: Fallen stones can lie on the road after they drop from the rock face.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the right, so stones come from the right.
explain.trap: 'presenza di pietre' (stones present): the result of falling rocks.

sceneParams.caption: Stones may be on the road

q19397.en: The sign shown warns of the danger of stones falling from the rock face.

explain.short: The black shape is a rock face, and the dots are stones falling from it.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the right, so stones come from the right.
explain.trap: 'parete rocciosa' (rock face): the black shape in the picture.

sceneParams.caption: Stones fall from the rock face

q19398.en: When you see the sign shown, it is wise to reduce speed to avoid hitting any rocks fallen on the carriageway.

explain.short: Going slowly lets you see and avoid a stone in time.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the right, so stones come from the right.
explain.trap: 'opportuno' (wise): slowing down is the right reaction here.

sceneParams.caption: Slow down to avoid fallen rocks

q19399.en: When you see the sign shown, you must watch out for possible sudden braking by the vehicles in front.

explain.short: A driver ahead may brake hard to avoid a stone, so keep distance and attention.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the right, so stones come from the right.
explain.trap: 'brusche frenate' (sudden braking): a stone on the road makes others brake.

q19400.en: The sign shown warns of a slippery stretch of road.

explain.short: A slippery road has its own sign (a skidding car); this one shows falling rocks.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the right, so stones come from the right.
explain.trap: 'sdrucciolevole' (slippery) is a different sign.

q19401.en: The sign shown warns of a narrowing on the right.

explain.short: A narrowing has its own sign with converging lines; here the black shape is a rock face.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the right, so stones come from the right.
explain.trap: 'strettoia a destra' (narrowing on the right): the black shape is not a road edge.

q19402.en: The sign shown warns of an unpaved stretch of road.

explain.short: The sign is about stones falling from a rock face, not about the road surface.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the right, so stones come from the right.
explain.trap: 'non asfaltato' (unpaved): nothing in the picture is about asphalt.

sceneParams.caption: Falling rocks, not an unpaved road

q19403.en: The sign shown warns of soft verges.

explain.short: Soft verges have their own sign; this one shows a rock face and falling stones.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the right, so stones come from the right.
explain.trap: 'banchine cedevoli' (soft verges, edges that sink) is a different danger.

q19404.en: The sign shown warns of a stretch of road where you cannot drive faster than 30 km/h.

explain.short: A danger sign gives no speed limit; a limit needs a round sign with the number.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the right, so stones come from the right.
explain.trap: '30 km/h': no number appears on this sign.

sceneParams.caption: Slow down - but no fixed limit

q19405.en: The sign shown warns of possible hailstorms.

explain.short: The falling dots are stones from the rock face, not hail.
explain.rule: 'Caduta massi' (falling rocks) is a danger sign; here the rock face is on the right, so stones come from the right.
explain.trap: 'grandinate' (hailstorms): the dots are stones, not hailstones.
